transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I've just completed your post-cataract surgery follow-up check. 

Do you have any questions about your surgery or how you're getting on with your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Yes, I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great question! You can start doing light exercise like gardening about 1 week after your surgery. However, you should avoid any strenuous or heavy exercise for a month.

Just be careful to avoid getting water in your eyes, especially in that first month.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do. When can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Good question. If you were using eye gel for dry eyes before your operation, it's safe to continue using it unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

If you're not sure about the specific timing or have concerns, I'd recommend checking with your GP or care team.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I do, actually. I'm very sensitive to bright light right now. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended:
Yes, that's quite normal! It's common for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses.

If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you go outside. However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to check it further. In that case, do let us know.

Do you have any other questions?
transcript.delivered:
Yes, that's quite normal! It's common for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's common to have some blurriness in the first week after surgery, and this should improve quickly and settle down over time.

How long has it been since your operation? If your vision is still quite blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything's okay.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, I think that covers everything I was wondering about. Thank you for all the information, Dora!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're welcome! Just to confirm - have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, all my questions have been answered. Thank you again!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! Take care, and best of luck with your recovery.
